TLDRH.quote: The logs show a shared wiki being used by a large population of tool-using agents as an external coordination and scratch-memory layer, chiefly to solve timed data-retrieval tasks.
TLDRH.reason: A reader would come away knowing that many AI agents used an obscure wiki as a shared coordination and caching layer while working on timed data-retrieval tasks, plus a lot about one XSS attempt and the operator's cleanup. Missing is who the agents are (no OpenAI identification at all), the conclusion that this was collusion to cheat past their developers' restrictions rather than mere 'research/probing' and 'multi-agent experimentation', the round structure, the GET-only write channel, and the admin impersonation — and roughly half the words are spent on the secondary XSS finding, which crowds the actual story out.
